1930.statement: Under Lilly's Alkindus attribution, ascendant lord applying to seventh lord is an argument marriage is performed; the printed margin adds the converse seventh-to-first application.
1930.precondition: Application of the specified first and seventh lords; the text does NOT restrict this item to trine/sextile.
1930.limit: The later discussion of trine or sextile must not be projected back into this broad statement.

1931.statement: Moon applying to Venus, with Venus strong and increasing in motion and in her own dignity, and the Moon likewise in dignity, is one Alkindus-attributed sign of completion.
1931.precondition: Venus is described as strong and increasing in motion and dignified, and Moon likewise dignified; Moon applies to Venus.
1931.limit: Do not shift Venus' motion condition exclusively onto the Moon.

1932.statement: Venus beholds Sun AND Sun has some dignity in the ascendant AND Sun beholds the lord of its own sign/dispositor; these are presented as a single marriage-completion testimony.
1932.precondition: All three conditions are joined by AND; the Sun's aspect target is lord of Sun's own sign, not the ascendant lord by default.
1932.limit: Earlier draft wrongly treated requirements as OR and replaced the Sun's dispositor with first lord.

1933.statement: If the applying planet and the planet it applies TO are both cadent, especially if their dispositors do not behold them, hopes exist at first but delaying and dragging may end with no marriage.
1933.precondition: An application EXISTS; both parties to it are cadent and dispositors' regard qualifies the verdict.
1933.limit: Earlier 'not regarding one another' reversed the first premise; this is not a judgment on no contact.

1934.statement: Under Alkindus, Moon, Sun, Venus and the lords of first and seventh in angles and mutually regarding (or beheld by their dispositors), even by hard aspect, are said to show initial despair but eventual marriage by consent of all parties.
1934.precondition: Named significators and angularity; mutual regard OR regard by their own lords, including possible square/opposition.
1934.limit: Consent by parties and the alternative dispositor-aspect condition are source conditions, not evidence of actual consent.

1937.statement: In the section on marriage taking effect, seventh lord placed in first or applying to first lord is printed as the sought party consenting UNWILLINGLY, despite a neighbouring paragraph suggesting goodwill.
1937.precondition: Seventh lord in first OR applying to first lord; retain the original printed word 'unwillingly'.
1937.limit: Source PDF338/printed304 explicitly says 'unwillingly'; no p304 erratum. This conflicts with p303 goodwill and could be a printer error, but no silent emendation is authorized.

1938.statement: Ascendant lord or Moon applying to seventh lord, or placed in seventh, is said to produce marriage through the querent's own labour.
1938.precondition: First lord/Moon applying to seventh lord OR in seventh; laborious completion is the proposed outcome.
1938.limit: Do not contrast this with an invented straightforward willing-consent implication from R1937, whose printed word is unwillingly.

1940.statement: Moon in the TENTH is said to signify mediation by friends; Moon applying to Venus is another friend-mediated route, and Sun applying to Venus, especially when Sun has seventh-house dignity, likewise furthers marriage.
1940.precondition: Three printed alternatives: Moon in tenth; Moon applying Venus; Sun applying Venus with special Sun seventh dignity.
1940.limit: The original reads tenth, not seventh, for the lunar placement. The Sun and Venus clause is distinct.

1949.statement: Interchangeable essential dignities of the signifiers, explained in the printed margin as one in the other's terms and another in triplicity or similar, are proposed as a completion sign; across page turn the Moon in seventh gives virtue to first or seventh lord.
1949.precondition: Exchange of signifiers' dignities OR Moon in seventh transferring virtue to the appropriate first/seventh lord.
1949.limit: No Sun-or-Venus angular exchange appears at this location; earlier record invented it.

1961.statement: Original-volume erratum instructs deletion of the printed conjunction symbol from the marriage-aspect comparison. Thus SQUARE or OPPOSITION implies much ado; TRINE or SEXTILE eases completion; RECEPTION is best.
1961.precondition: A marriage otherwise promised by one of the specified aspects; the conjunction token is explicitly deleted by printed305 line22 erratum.
1961.limit: Original PDF339 still prints the conjunction glyph; errata PDF888 says 'p305 l22 dele [conjunction]'. Preserve both witnesses and the approximate line-count difference.

1963.statement: Despite seeming probability of marriage, an EVIL planet may obstruct reception between signifiers, frustrate their intended aspect, prohibit it, or interject rays between them; inspect the evil planet for the alleged obstacle.
1963.precondition: Existing favourable marriage indications notwithstanding, a specifically harmful planet prevents reception, perfection, or interposes its rays.
1963.limit: The original does NOT here call beneficial translation of light the obstruction; earlier draft reversed the mechanism.

1967.statement: Fifth-house lord used as obstacle may raise objections about children if either party has any; in a bachelor question rumours or FEARS about fertility, prior offspring or sexual misconduct may be voiced, including scandal rather than established facts. Apply analogously if a woman asks.
1967.precondition: The fifth lord is the relevant hindering planet; distinguish child-present scenario from a bachelor's question and all claims as others' objections or fears.
1967.limit: The source says 'perhaps it is objected', 'scandalized', and 'feared'; no actual infertility, offspring, infidelity or lechery is verified. 'Luxury' is historical sexual indulgence, not material luxury.

1992.statement: For the woman, Lilly judges by the planet the SUN beholds: SUN in trine/sextile of SATURN implies wise and painstaking/diligent; SUN aspecting JUPITER implies honest. A different earlier Moon–Venus clause concerns the man.
1992.precondition: Question concerns characterization of the woman and the Sun's trine/sextile to Saturn OR Sun aspect to Jupiter, separately.
1992.limit: Earlier draft wrongly put Moon with Mars and misinterpreted 'painfull' as causing pain rather than industrious/diligent.

2013.statement: An INFORTUNE IN THE FOURTH (following the tenth-house malefic example) is said to signify divorce, willingness to divorce, or hindrance concerning dowry.
2013.precondition: A malefic/infortune physically PLACED in fourth house, not merely fourth-house ruler afflicted.
2013.limit: Preserve all three alternatives; original draft omitted divorce and changed house placement to ruler affliction.

2018.statement: In 'Who shall be the cause of their Strife, or the authour of their Good', Moon TRINE or SEXTILE good planets predicts gifts from friends; Moon SQUARE good planets signifies benefit 'by dead men'; Moon CONJUNCT good planets suggests benefit by the spouses' own industry and labour.
2018.precondition: Specific lunar aspect to good planet: trine/sextile vs square vs bodily conjunction each carries different source outcome.
2018.limit: No opposition or quarrel outcome appears in this clause. This is historical money/benefit interpretation, not independently observed death or gifts.

2028.statement: The printed Arabic aphorism concerns Moon in the first TWELVE DEGREES OF CAPRICORN for one espoused to a wife: it says he will lose her before marriage, or die within six months, or live in discord with her.
2028.precondition: Moon in Capricorn 0°–12° AND a person espoused to a wife; three alternative author-reported outcomes.
2028.limit: The printed sign is Capricorn, not Virgo. Original margin cautions not to trust such Arabic aphorisms without corroborating significators; no mortality outcomes verified.
